I have farmed this land since I was young. My husband passed years ago, and my son went to work in Shijiazhuang. I manage about 4 mu myself, sometimes my neighbor's son helps with the heavier work.

Here in Quzhou, everyone grows wheat and corn. I grow wheat and corn. My mother grew wheat and corn. The land here is flat, the water is underground, and the markets in the county town buy both. I would not know how to grow something else, and I would not trust myself to learn at my age.

For the wheat, I will plant in October after I prepare the ground with the rotary machine — my nephew borrows a tractor for me. I will buy seed from the village supply station, the kind they always sell there, the improved kind that does well here. I will put down fertilizer at planting and again in spring. I always water before winter sets in, then again when the stalks are growing tall, then once more near heading. I spray for weeds early on and check for rust later.

After wheat harvest in June I will plant corn right away — no time to waste, no need to plow again. Corn seed I always buy hybrid, everyone does now. I will fertilize twice. I water if it does not rain enough in July or August. Corn does not need much from me. I harvest in September and sell most of it.

I do not experiment. At my age, a bad harvest means real trouble.
